text:
Alex: Kicking off a small canary for nova-7b-v2 in us-west-2 at 17:00 PT. Deploybot will do staged traffic shifts 1% -> 5% -> 10% over 30m. Please monitor latency, error-rate, and hallucination evals. Gating thresholds: 99p latency < 1200ms, 5m error rate < 0.5%. If breached at any stage, rollback to nova-7b-v1 and pin.
Mira: noted. I added the preflight checklist to the rollout doc and pinned the telemetry panels. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nova-7b-v2-canary
Samir: FYI heap growth on this family tends to spike at ~2k tokens. Watch for OOMs on the 32G nodes. If memory climbs, switch to quantv1 variant or reduce batch size.
Tasha: Who's drafting the release notes snippet for product? Need a short blurb for the API changelog and a migration note for pinned clients.
Alex: I'll do the short blurb. Draft: "nova-7b-v2: improved instruction-following and lower latency on typical prompts. Pin to nova-7b-v1 to opt out of the update." Will push to the release-notes page in 15m.
Ryan: Add fallback ordering to the catalog entry: [nova-7b-v2, nova-7b-v1, titan-lite]. Confirmed compatibility for model variants (tokenizer and output schema)?
Mira: Confirmed. Small behaviour diffs expected, but schema and tool-calling preserved. Added a note to run the smoke eval suite (promptset: canary-smoke-2026) against the canary traffic.
deploybot: deploybot: canary start scheduled at 2026-03-21T17:00:00Z. Will report each stage. /deploy start --catalog nova-7b-v2 --region us-west-2 --ladder 1,5,10 --check telemetry
Samir: Also enable prefix caching on these routes — should cut token compute by ~12% and reduce p99.
Alex: Good call. Mira, can you enable caching for the mobile-api and web-handoff routes in the config? It needs to be on before 17:00.
Mira: Enabled caching for mobile-api and web-handoff. Config snippet: ```routes:
  - name: mobile-api
    cache: prefix
  - name: web-handoff
    cache: prefix``` Deployed to staging, will push to prod immediately after canary go-ahead.
sre-bot: alert rule created: catalog.canary.latency.p99.us-west-2 > 1200ms for 5m -> severity: high -> channel: #incidents
Tasha: For rollback comms, let's set the standard line: "Rolling back nova-7b-v2 to nova-7b-v1 due to canary SLA breach. Follow-up postmortem will be scheduled." I'll add to the incident template.
deploybot: Stage 1 complete: 1% traffic -> OK. telemetry snapshot: latency.p99=980ms, errors=0.12%, mem-avg=21.3GB
Alex: Thanks. Move to 5% when ready.
deploybot: Stage 2 complete: 5% traffic -> OK. telemetry snapshot: latency.p99=1100ms, errors=0.28%, mem-avg=22.1GB
Samir: mem growth looks linear but within margin. Keeping an eye.
deploybot: Stage 3 in 10m: intended 10% traffic. ETA now +10m.
Ryan: Quick decision note: if hallucination regression exceeds 2% on the canary-smoke prompts, we rollback even if SLOs look fine.
Mira: Ran a sample of canary-smoke-2026 last hour against the canary cluster — hallucination delta = +0.9% vs v1. Not ideal, but under the 2% tolerance.
Alex: If we see hallucination >2% at 10% traffic, we rollback and mark for targeted quality tuning. Everyone ok with that policy?
All: :thumbsup:
deploybot: Stage 3 complete: 10% traffic -> borderline on quality. telemetry snapshot: latency.p99=1250ms, errors=0.45%, hallucination_delta=2.6%
Alex: We're breaching latency and hallucination gates. Initiating rollback to nova-7b-v1. Deploybot, execute rollback and pin nova-7b-v1 for the catalog entry.
deploybot: rollback initiated -> switching routes back to nova-7b-v1; applying pin: catalog.pin=nova-7b-v1
deploybot: rollback complete. snapshot after rollback: latency.p99=990ms, errors=0.15%, mem-avg=20.9GB, hallucination_delta back to baseline
Mira: Marking this canary as failed in the rollout doc, capturing telemetry and sample prompts that triggered hallucinations. Saving artifacts: s3://redwood-canary-artifacts/nova7b-v2/1749991234/
Samir: I captured a heap profile from a 32G node during the 10% stage; uploading now. Looks like a spike correlated with a long-context batch.
Tasha: I'll file the release notes PR as "postponed: nova-7b-v2" and add the rollback rationale. Also scheduling a follow-up sync with research and infra for root cause tomorrow 10am PT.
Ryan: For next attempt, propose: 1) tune quant profile to reduce memory, 2) run expanded hallucination evals against 10k prompts, 3) smaller step to 7% instead of 10%.
Alex: Agreed. Thanks team. Closing this thread — tracking action items in the rollout doc and follow-up meeting invite sent.
Mira: +1. I'll also add a temporary routing rule to prefer titan-lite for mobile-api until nova-7b-v2 is revalidated.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0423 - nova-7b-v2 canary SLA breach. Assigned: Samir, Mira, Alex. Severity: medium.
Alex: tagging product and support for visibility: @Tasha @Ryan
Tasha: Thx. I'll prepare the external customer note if needed.
